To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the last six amino acids of the carboxyl cytoplasmic domain of CD36 are required for OxLDL binding and uptake, and this region is not involved in the binding of the anti-CD36 mAb 10/5.
the terminal six amino-acid residues (K472STOP) of the CD36 cytosolic tail are critical to its binding and internalization function.
a six amino-acid sequence at the C-terminal end of CD36 cytoplamic tail, containing the last six amino acids of the cytoplamic tail (RKKKRR), is required for OxLDL binding and internalization.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of a new functional domain on the cytoplamic tail of CD36, implicated in the binding, capture, and internalization of OxLDL, and the subsequent degradation of the oxidized lipid particles.

a new domain of a major scavenger receptor, CD36, which is involved in the binding and uptake of OxLDL and which is localized in the last six amino acids of the carboxyl terminus of the CD36 cytosolic tail.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms involved in the OxLDL-CD36 interaction, and may contribute to our understanding of the mechanisms involved in the development of atherosclerotic lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the last six amino acids of CD36 cytoplamic tail are involved in the binding of OxLDL, but not in its subsequent internalization and degradation.
the last six amino acids of the CD36 cytosolic tail are essential to the binding, internalisation and degradation of Ox-LDL.
the terminal six amino-acid residues of the CD36 carboxy cytosolic tail contain a functional domain that is implicated in the binding, internalisation and degradation of Ox-LDL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the terminal six amino-acid of the carboxyl cytoplasmic region of CD36 is the functional domain implicated in OxLDL binding.
the last six amino acids of the carboxyl cytoplasmic domain of CD36 are essential for OxLDL capture and internalization.

the last six amino acids of the carboxyl cytoplasmic domain of CD36 are critical for OxLDL binding, internalization, and degradation, whereas the last amino-acids of this domain do not play a role in the binding of an anti- CD36 mAb (10/5).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the last six amino acids of the CD36 tail, which is the minimal sequence necessary for OxLDL binding, is not required for the binding of a mAb (10/5).
CD36 is an important molecule for OxLDL uptake and the terminal six amino-acid residues of the carboxyl cytoplasmic domain are essential for this process.
